descriptionChirho: A young child or infant, emphasizing tender age rather than social role; used of baby Moses in the basket, the child Samuel, Ishmael as a boy, and newborns or small children generally (Arabic صَبِيٌّ, Korean 아이/어린이, Swahili mtoto, Hindi बच्चा/बालक, Spanish niño).

A youth, adolescent, or young man of vigorous age; emphasizes stage of life between childhood and full maturity, used of young warriors, the young Absalom, Joseph as a seventeen-year-old, and groups of young men generally (Arabic فَتًى/شَابّ/غُلَام, Korean 젊은이/소년, Swahili kijana/vijana, Hindi जवान, Spanish joven/muchacho).

A personal servant, attendant, or retainer serving a master; includes armor-bearers, household attendants (like Gehazi serving Elisha), and young men in the service of a lord or lady, typically with possessive suffix 'his/her/my servant(s)' (Arabic غُلَام with possessive, Korean 종/하인/사환, Swahili mtumishi, Hindi सेवक/नौकर, Spanish siervo/criado).

Used in the temporal expression 'from (one's) youth' (מִנַּעַר / מִנְּעֻרָיו), indicating the time period of childhood or early life as a point of origin, meaning 'since I/he was young' (Arabic مِن صَغِيرٍ, Korean 에서 어린이, Swahili kutoka kijana, Hindi बालक से/जवान से, Spanish desde joven).
